Here are the search results for De-An Huang, NVIDIA researcher:

## Personal Websites & Profiles

**Personal Academic Website (Stanford):**
- https://ai.stanford.edu/~dahuang/ — His main personal website hosted at Stanford AI Lab. Contact: dahuang [at] cs [dot] stanford [dot] edu

**NVIDIA Research Pages:**
- https://research.nvidia.com/person/de-an-huang — Main NVIDIA Research profile page
- https://research.nvidia.com/labs/lpr/author/de-an-huang/ — NVIDIA Learning and Perception Research lab page
- https://research.nvidia.com/labs/genair/author/de-an-huang/ — Fundamental Generative AI Research lab page
- https://research.nvidia.com/labs/srl/authors/de-an-huang/ — NVIDIA Seattle Robotics Lab page

**Google Scholar:**
- https://scholar.google.com/citations?hl=en&user=HEY3UzgAAAAJ

## Background

De-An Huang is affiliated with Stanford University with research interests in Computer Vision, Robotics, Machine Learning, and Bioinformatics. He was also a past NVIDIA Graduate Fellow while at Stanford University.

He has interned with Dieter Fox at NVIDIA Seattle Robotics Lab, Vignesh Ramanathan and Dhruv Mahajan at Facebook Applied Machine Learning, Zicheng Liu at Microsoft Research Redmond, and Leonid Sigal at Disney Research Pittsburgh.

## Notable Recent Research

His recent publications span vision-language models, video understanding, and generative AI, including:
- **FRAG: Frame Selection Augmented Generation for Long Video and Long Document Understanding** (with Subhashree Radhakrishnan, Zhiding Yu, Jan Kautz)
- **Eagle 2.5: Boosting Long-Context Post-Training for Frontier Vision-Language Models** (a large NVIDIA collaboration)
- **MinVIS: A Minimal Video Instance Segmentation Framework without Video-based Training** (NeurIPS 2022) and **MineDojo: Building Open-Ended Embodied Agents with Internet-Scale Knowledge** (NeurIPS 2022 Dataset & Benchmark)
- **I2SB: Image-to-Image Schrödinger Bridge** with Guan-Horng Liu, Arash Vahdat, Evangelos Theodorou, Weili Nie, and Anima Anandkumar (ICML July 2023)

His frequent collaborators at NVIDIA include Jan Kautz, Zhiding Yu, Anima Anandkumar, Arash Vahdat, and Pavlo Molchanov.

Here's a summary of what I found about Linxi "Jim" Fan and his personal website:

## Personal Website
His personal website is **https://jimfan.me**. It is described as the "Official Website of Dr. Linxi 'Jim' Fan, AI Research Scientist," where he notes he obtained his Ph.D. in Computer Science from Stanford, advised by Fei-Fei Li, with a primary focus on developing generally capable autonomous agents.

## Current Role at NVIDIA
According to his website, he is a Senior Research Scientist at NVIDIA and Lead of the AI Agents Initiative, with a mission to build generally capable agents across physical worlds (robotics) and virtual worlds (games, simulation).

His LinkedIn profile lists more advanced titles: NVIDIA Director of AI & Distinguished Scientist, Co-Lead of Project GR00T (Humanoid Robotics) & GEAR Lab, Stanford Ph.D., OpenAI's first intern, working on Physical AGI.

## Background & Education
- He obtained his Ph.D. at Stanford Vision Lab, advised by Prof. Fei-Fei Li, and previously interned at OpenAI (with Ilya Sutskever and Andrej Karpathy), Baidu AI Labs (with Andrew Ng and Dario Amodei), and MILA (with Yoshua Bengio).
- He graduated as the Valedictorian of Class 2016 and received the Illig Medal at Columbia University.

## Research Focus
His research explores the bleeding edge of multimodal foundation models, reinforcement learning, computer vision, and large-scale systems.

## Notable Projects
He spearheaded Voyager (the first AI agent that plays Minecraft proficiently and bootstraps its capabilities continuously), MineDojo (open-ended agent learning by watching 100,000s of Minecraft YouTube videos), and Eureka.

## Awards & Recognition
His publications have won several awards and nominations, including the Outstanding Paper Award at NeurIPS 2022 for "MineDojo," and his works have been featured by media such as New York Times, Forbes, MIT Technology Review, TechCrunch, and WIRED.

## Other Online Profiles
- **NVIDIA Research page:** https://research.nvidia.com/person/linxi-jim-fan
- **Twitter/X:** @DrJimFan
- **LinkedIn:** linkedin.com/in/drjimfan/
- **Google Scholar:** Available under user ID sljtWIUAAAAJ

Here are the search results for Anima Anandkumar's Caltech personal website:

## Personal Website
Her personal/research website is hosted at: **http://tensorlab.cms.caltech.edu/users/anima** (Tensorlab at Caltech CMS)

## Caltech Faculty Profile Pages
She has multiple official Caltech profile pages across different departments (since she holds appointments in several):

- **Computing + Mathematical Sciences (CMS)**: https://www.cms.caltech.edu/people/anima
- **Engineering and Applied Science (EAS)**: https://www.eas.caltech.edu/people/anima
- **Biology and Biological Engineering**: https://www.bbe.caltech.edu/people/anima-anandkumar
- **Medical Engineering**: https://mede.caltech.edu/people/anima
- **Chen Institute for Neuroscience**: https://neuroscience.caltech.edu/people/anima-anandkumar
- **Center for Sensing to Intelligence**: https://s2i.caltech.edu/people/anima-anandkumar
- **IQIM**: https://iqim.caltech.edu/profile/anima-anandkumar/
- **Caltech Directory**: https://directory.caltech.edu/personnel/anima

## About Her
Anima Anandkumar holds dual positions in academia and industry. She is a Bren professor at Caltech CMS department and a director of machine learning research at NVIDIA. At NVIDIA, she is leading the research group that develops next-generation AI algorithms.

Her academic background: B.S., Indian Institutes of Technology, 2004; Ph.D., Cornell University, 2009; Visiting Associate, Caltech, 2017; Bren Professor, 2017-.

## Research Focus
Anima Anandkumar has made fundamental contributions to AI that is revolutionizing scientific modeling and discovery. She invented Neural Operators for learning multiscale phenomena that frequently occur in nature, such as fluid dynamics, material modeling and wave propagation. She employed Neural Operators to train the first AI-based high-resolution weather model. It is tens of thousands of times faster than existing physics-based forecasting, and is running at premier weather agencies.

Her AI algorithms have enabled many other scientific advances such as modeling plasma evolution in nuclear fusion, enabling safer autonomous drone flights, and designing novel medical devices, drugs, and functional enzymes.

Her primary research areas include AI algorithms, AI+Science, Neural Operators, PDE, and Tensor Methods.

Her contact info from the Caltech directory: Office: Annenberg IST Center, WORK MC 305-16 Pasadena CA 91125 USA, Office Phone: 626-395-2291.

The most likely "personal website" you're looking for is the **Tensorlab page** at tensorlab.cms.caltech.edu/users/anima, which serves as her main research group homepage.
